records.name: Cellular kinetics and persistence
records.tldr: A living cell therapy can change its number, location and state after administration. The starting dose, a sampled cell count and useful function are different measurements.
records.summary: After a cell infusion, measured abundance depends on division, survival and redistribution. In vivo engineering may also continue to generate newly engineered cells. A blood sample describes one compartment and time; it cannot count all cells in the body or establish entry into a tumor. Detectable receptor-encoding sequences, viable receptor-positive cells, persistent markers and functional activity should be reported separately.

NCI: T-cell transfer therapy and harms
Liu et al.: one cord-blood CAR-NK construct in lymphoid tumors (2020)

notes: FDA CAR T-cell guidance treats exposure/kinetics, pharmacodynamic response, immunogenicity, identity, viability and potency as distinct assessments. Blood concentration-time measurements and optional disease-tissue sampling answer different distribution questions. A sequence assay is not automatically a count of viable cells expressing a functional surface receptor.

Keep the measurement method, time, compartment, units and denominator attached. A receptor-positive percentage can fall while absolute receptor-positive cells per microliter remain unchanged if the sampled denominator increases. Neither measure alone establishes an unchanged total-body cell population, tumor entry or antitumor benefit.

An administered cell dose is an input. The dose of a vector or particle used for in vivo engineering does not directly specify the later number of engineered cells. Autologous means the recipient’s own cells; allogeneic means cells from another person. Engineering outside versus inside the body is a separate axis; a prepared delivery product can engineer the recipient's own cells.

Expansion and persistence can prolong useful activity or harmful recognition. Stopping further administration does not instantly remove living cells or reverse an injury already triggered. A safety switch addresses a specified control mechanism; cell elimination, receptor shutoff and treatment of downstream inflammation are different interventions.

In the Liu cord-blood CAR-NK study, low-level detection at least 12 months after treatment belonged to a construct with IL-15 and an inducible caspase-9 switch. It does not establish the behavior of every NK-cell source or equate marker detection with continuing useful function.

In a fictional pair of matched blood samples, 20 per cent of 100 viable T cells per microlitre and 10 per cent of 200 both give 20 receptor-positive viable T cells per microlitre. The percentage fell because its denominator doubled; the concentration did not. This conclusion requires comparable collection, volume and viable-cell gates. It says nothing about the total number of cells in the body, tumour entry or continued target-cell killing. Genetic copies, surface receptor, viable cells and useful function remain separate measurements.

Cells respond biologically to signals, without intention; more cells do not by themselves establish better or safer treatment. Consider two fictional ready-made products: a carrier that gives receptor instructions to the recipient’s own T cells, and a prepared batch of donor-derived engineered cells. The first can generate autologous cells in vivo; the second supplies allogeneic cells engineered ex vivo. State four things separately: the starting cell family, whose cells they are, where engineering happens and whether cells or an instruction carrier are administered. Neither card establishes available supply, the final engineered-cell population or treatment benefit. NK and NKT name different cell families; an added receptor does not erase the recipient cell’s other inputs.

A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

Compare time courses rather than labels when interpreting reversibility. Antibodies also take time to clear after dosing stops. In an engineered-cell product, carrier exposure, instructions, receptor protein, living cells and inflammation can have different durations. Stopping the next administration, reducing one signal, removing the cells and reversing an established injury are separate claims.

records.name: Ex vivo cell expansion
records.tldr: Cell expansion increases the number of a defined group of living cells outside the body. Selecting cells or activating them answers a different question.
records.summary: Expansion compares absolute counts of a specified living population at stated points in a culture process. Enrichment or selection changes mixture composition, while activation changes cellular state. Measurements need a consistent cell definition, viability basis, sampling method and interval. Cell concentration can change with dilution or volume, and a higher fraction can result from losing other cells rather than producing more intended cells.

links.label: FDA: CAR T-cell development guidance, January 2024
Ghassemi et al., 2018: defined culture-duration comparisons and mouse experiments
Dupouy et al., 2022: factory expansion and adult CALM cellular kinetics

notes: In a fictional mixture, 20 million intended cells and 80 million other cells become 20 million intended and five million other cells after enrichment. The intended fraction rises from 20/100 to 20/25 without increasing the intended-cell count. In a separate culture example, 20 million viable intended cells becoming 100 million is five-fold expansion. These are invented arithmetic examples, not process-performance targets.

Culture conditions, activation, gene transfer, duration, selection and preservation can change subsets, differentiation, viability and function. A greater count does not establish equal starting-cell quality, a favourable state or greater tumour killing. Activation markers and intended biological activity require suitable separate measurements.

Ghassemi's 2018 study compared shorter and longer preparation in human CAR T-cell experiments, a mouse acute-lymphoblastic-leukaemia model and manufacturing-feasibility work. The reported culture comparison does not prove that every shorter process improves human outcomes or specify one optimal duration for all products.

Dupouy's adult CALM analysis distinguishes factory fold expansion from later blood transgene and flow-cytometry kinetics. In-body detection depends on sampling, proliferation, distribution, loss and expression. A blood copy count is not an absolute whole-body count or a direct functional assay.

Expansion can be one input to a product-specific control strategy. It does not replace identity, purity, viability, potency, contamination testing, lot disposition or clinical readiness. Manufacturing yield, culture time, collection-to-infusion time and patient benefit remain separate outcomes.

records.name: CAR-NK & CAR-macrophage
records.tldr: CAR-NK cells and CAR-macrophages add recognition receptors to different innate immune-cell families. Their native functions, starting materials and engineered support still matter.
records.summary: A CAR adds a recognition input rather than replacing the effector cell. NK cells retain activating and inhibitory receptor inputs; macrophages have different functions, including phagocytosis and antigen handling. Donor blood, cord blood, pluripotent-cell-derived products and NK cell lines are distinct starting materials. Product-specific manufacture, expansion, persistence, tissue access, compatibility and harms need their own evidence. A small favorable blood-cancer study does not rank every NK product as safer than every T-cell product or establish solid-tumor benefit.

Klichinsky et al., Human chimeric antigen receptor macrophages for cancer immunotherapy (Nature Biotechnology 2020)
Tang et al.: irradiated CD33-CAR NK-92 cells in an early AML study (2018)
Karre et al.: reduced self-MHC and rejection in mouse lymphoma models (1986)

notes: In the 11-patient Liu study, cord-blood CD19 CAR-NK cells also encoded IL-15 and inducible caspase-9. No cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity or graft-versus-host disease was observed in that cohort, and low-level cells remained detectable for at least 12 months. This is neither proof of zero risk nor evidence for a uniformly short lifespan across CAR-NK platforms.

NK-92 is a continuously growing cell line, not a donor primary-cell preparation. Tang used CD33-CAR NK-92 cells irradiated with 10 Gy before infusion in an early AML study. Irradiation to limit proliferation makes its persistence question different from that of a cytokine-supported cord-blood product; the irradiation dose is not a universal CAR-NK treatment dose.

Reduced HLA display can reduce some inhibitory NK inputs, but activating signals, NK education and the actual cell-target pair still matter. CAR recognition, native NK activity and missing-self recognition are different inputs. An NK cell is not a natural killer T cell, and absence of a conventional TCR does not remove every compatibility, rejection or product-contamination concern.

Compare matched engineered and unmodified effector cells with target-positive and target-negative cells; retain donor/source, cell ratio and observation time. Attribution to a native receptor needs an independent perturbation with controls for changes in other ligands and target-cell viability. Binding, cytokine or granule release, viable-cell abundance and completed killing should not be substituted for one another.

Klichinsky engineered human macrophages and studied antigen-specific phagocytosis, inflammatory changes and tumor effects in cell and mouse models. These results describe a macrophage construct and those models; they do not establish a clinical efficacy or persistence ranking against CAR-NK or CAR-T.
records.principle: Add a specified CAR to an NK cell or macrophage and evaluate the receptor together with the cell family, source, engineering and native responses.
strengths: Different native effector functions can be investigated alongside CAR recognition
Some NK products have shown allogeneic feasibility in defined early studies
limitations: Persistence depends on source and engineered support
Host rejection, inflammatory harms and manufacturing quality remain product-specific questions
Cell and mouse results do not establish clinical benefit in solid tumors

records.name: Gamma-delta T cells
records.tldr: Gamma-delta T cells are a family of T cells whose receptor is built from different protein chains than most T cells, and different subsets recognise different signals, often without the usual peptide display. The family name does not say which signal a particular cell, or an engineered product, uses to find a tumour.
records.summary: The T-cell receptor of most T cells has alpha and beta chains; gamma-delta T cells have gamma and delta chains and also carry other activating and inhibitory receptors. They remain T cells and are distinct from natural killer cells. A review distinguishes gamma-delta from alpha-beta T cells partly by the antigens their receptors recognise, and notes that NKG2D is expressed by many gamma-delta subsets as well as by natural killer cells and CD8 T cells (Vantourout and Hayday, 2013). Names such as Vδ1 and Vγ9Vδ2 describe receptor variable regions and mark subsets that sit in different places. Healthy human breast tissue harboured a distinct gamma-delta compartment made mainly of Vδ1 cells, whereas Vδ2 cells predominate in blood; the breast Vδ1 cells could be activated innately through the NKG2D receptor, and in paired samples from 11 people with triple-negative breast cancer, progression-free and overall survival correlated with Vδ1 representation but not with total gamma-delta or Vδ2 cells (Wu et al., 2019). That is a small observational association in tissue biology and did not test an infused product.

notes: Recognition differs by subset, and it is not always free of HLA. For the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, which responds to phosphoantigens (small phosphorylated metabolites produced by microbes and overexpressed by some cancers), butyrophilin 2A1 (BTN2A1) binds the Vγ9 chain of the receptor, associates with a second butyrophilin, BTN3A1, and the two act together to start the response; a second ligand, possibly BTN3A1, binds a separate region that includes the Vδ2 chain (Rigau et al., 2020). This is not a peptide sitting in an HLA groove. HLA independence is also not universal: one characterised Vγ5Vδ1 receptor was restricted by HLA-A*24:02 and depended on the CD8-alpha co-receptor, acting on blood-cancer and solid-tumour cells in vitro and in vivo while sparing healthy tissue in those models (Kierkels et al., 2019). That receptor's mechanism is not an eligibility rule for the family.

An engineered receptor is a separate recognition route. Adding a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor to expanded human Vδ1 and Vδ2 cells increased GD2-specific killing of GD2-expressing cancer cell lines, did not impair movement towards tumour cells in vitro, and expanded Vδ2 cells kept the ability to take up tumour antigen and cross-present it to alpha-beta T cells (Capsomidis et al., 2018). That is a preclinical result for that preparation, and it does not show that any gamma-delta product enters tumours, cross-presents usefully or prevents antigen escape in patients. An allogeneic gamma-delta product that the registry names HLA-G-CAR.BiTE allogeneic γδ T cells (NCT06150885, phase 1 and 2) was listed as recruiting when the registry record was read for this entry; the record describes the product and the study design and reports no efficacy. A receptor added to a cell needs its own target on the tumour, HLA-low does not mean target-positive, and avoiding peptide presentation is not the same as avoiding antigen escape. Cells are identified by flow cytometry and receptor sequencing, but a response against one target line does not establish tumour entry, persistence or benefit, and matched cells without the added receptor are needed to separate native from engineered recognition. Two cautions are OnCo's reasoning and not findings of the cited papers: a product made of many receptor clones is not automatically broader or more effective than one defined clone, and the name gamma-delta describes the receptor chains and not the cell source, so whether cells came from the patient or from a donor has to be stated separately.

Measurement separates identity, repertoire and function. Sanz et al. (2023) used flow cytometry to isolate human gamma-delta subsets and assessed receptor repertoires separately from cytotoxicity. Their Daudi-cell cocultures included target-only and effector-only controls; degranulation, granzyme or perforin measurements and target-cell death were distinct readouts. These are results for defined human subsets and laboratory targets, not a universal assay or a test of tumour entry in patients.

For interpretation, report the parent population, percentage and any valid absolute count with the specimen and sampling method. Receptor-sequence abundance does not identify the receptor ligand. Rigau et al. (2020) established a defined BTN2A1-dependent recognition mechanism for the Vgamma9Vdelta2 phosphoantigen response; that specificity is an example of why innate-like does not mean nonspecific. To test native versus added-receptor recognition, compare matched cells without the added receptor, target-positive and target-negative cells, and a suitable receptor-blocking or target-perturbation condition. Keep relevant healthy-cell controls, viability and exposure conditions explicit. This is experimental-design reasoning from the separate recognition mechanisms, not a claim that one cited assay validates every product. HLA loss does not establish that the native ligand or the added receptor target is present, and two recognition routes do not prove escape prevention.

records.name: In vivo CAR-T
records.tldr: An in vivo delivery product carries receptor-encoding instructions into cells inside the body. Its dose is different from the later number and activity of engineered cells.
records.summary: Targeted delivery can supply CAR-encoding instructions to cells inside the body, using formats such as a viral vector or an mRNA lipid nanoparticle. This changes where engineering happens; it does not mean the active cells are donor-derived. Delivery targeting, cancer-antigen recognition, generated-cell abundance, receptor duration and useful function are separate questions. Conditioning, repeat dosing, safety and total cost belong to a specified product and protocol rather than to the in vivo label.

links.label: Pfeiffer et al., In vivo generation of human CD19-CAR T cells results in B-cell depletion and signs of cytokine release syndrome (EMBO Molecular Medicine 2018)
Rurik et al.: targeted mRNA nanoparticles in a mouse cardiac-injury model (2022)
ClinicalTrials.gov: INT2104 phase 1 oncology design, not an outcome report
FDA: CAR T-cell development guidance, January 2024
Hunter et al., 2025: human-cell, humanised-mouse and monkey experiments
In vivo generation of human CD19-CAR T cells results in B-cell depletion and signs of cytokine release syndrome. (2018)
A targeting lentiviral vector for generation of CAR-T cells in vivo. (2026)

notes: Pfeiffer generated human CD19 CAR T cells with a CD8-targeted lentiviral vector in humanized mouse experiments. B-cell depletion and signs consistent with cytokine release syndrome were observed. This was a preclinical study, not a human clinical response report or evidence for freedom from inflammatory toxicity.

Rurik used targeted mRNA lipid nanoparticles to generate transient CAR T cells in a mouse cardiac-injury model. It demonstrates a delivery/expression approach in that setting; it does not establish cancer efficacy, human safety or an interchangeable regimen for other delivery formats.

The INT2104 registry NCT06539338 identifies a phase 1 B-cell-cancer study in the dated source check. A trial design or registry listing does not supply efficacy results, prove local slot availability or validate a platform-wide claim about conditioning.

A prepared carrier can engineer the recipient's own cells. Vector or nanoparticle dose, ongoing delivery, newly generated cells, cell proliferation and receptor persistence should be measured separately. Stopping carrier administration need not immediately end the activity of cells already engineered.

The cited preclinical results do not by themselves establish a fixed cost reduction, universal absence of lymphodepletion or automatic repeat-dose feasibility. Evaluate the actual process, monitoring and protocol rather than treating these as inherent benefits of all in vivo products.

Ex vivo describes engineering outside the body followed by administration of a cell product. In vivo engineering administers an instruction-carrying product and generates modified cells inside the body; it is not the same as testing an ex vivo product in an animal. Location, recipient versus donor origin and transient versus stable genetic fate are separate attributes.

In a fictional sampled population of 200 cells, 60 show the stated receptor measurement: 60/200 is 30% of that sampled population at that time. It does not specify a whole-body engineered-cell count, the administered carrier dose, tissue distribution, durable expression or killing. Sequence detection, expression, abundance and biological function need their own measurements.

Hunter's 2025 study used targeted mRNA nanoparticles in healthy-donor and autoimmune patient cell samples, humanised mice and cynomolgus monkeys. Tumour control in mice and B-cell depletion in monkeys are not human treatment outcomes. Quality testing of the administered carrier also cannot sample every subsequently engineered cell or tissue; relevant biodistribution, expression, kinetics and safety evidence is still needed.

Pfeiffer’s CD8-targeted lentiviral experiment used immunodeficient NSG mice engrafted with activated human blood mononuclear cells, with separate Raji-lymphoma conditions. Seven days after vector administration, CAR-positive cells represented 30 to 50 per cent of CD8 cells in peritoneal fluid, 10 to 35 per cent in spleen and 5 to 30 per cent in blood; fewer than 0.5 per cent of CD8-negative cells entered the CAR-positive gate. Vehicle and reporter-vector controls, CD19-cell depletion and the starting target-cell population mattered. These later fractions combine delivery with survival and antigen-driven expansion; they are not pure entry efficiencies, whole-body exclusivity or human efficacy results.

A fictional 48-hour sample contains receptor expression in 60 of 200 viable T cells and five of 100 non-T cells. That is 30 per cent of T cells and five per cent of non-T cells; about 92 per cent of all expressing cells are T cells (60 of 65). None of these denominators establishes exclusive delivery. Compare matched carrier/receptor controls, antigen-positive and antigen-negative targets and relevant healthy cells. Sampling time, cell recovery and viable gates stay attached; a culture sample does not enumerate every tissue.

A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

Consider a complete fictional evidence packet, not a real therapy. Carrier P is a T-cell-directed lipid nanoparticle containing mRNA for CAR-X, which recognises extracellular epitope E on antigen X, and a separate supportive receptor R activated by trigger D. R does not add a cancer target, and P has no cell-elimination mechanism. One human T-cell donor supplies the culture work and selected human components of the mouse model. All functional experiments use lot A; lots B and C have identity data only. The matched cellular comparator uses the same carrier, CAR-X and total RNA without R, with D-present, D-absent and D-alone controls only where specified.

In the fictional packet’s mixed-cell culture at 24 hours, 1,000 sampled viable cells include 100 T cells. RNA is detected in 60 T cells and 240 other cells; surface CAR in 50 T cells and 150 others; 40 T cells express both CAR and R. Unexposed controls are negative. CAR-positive T cells are 50/100, or 50 per cent of T cells, but T cells are 50/200, or 25 per cent of all CAR-positive cells. CAR-positive cells are 200/1,000, or 20 per cent of the whole sample; dual-positive T cells are 40/100, or 40 per cent of T cells. RNA, surface protein and coexpression are different readouts, and none measures killing or body-wide distribution.

In a second fictional card, wells start with 100 target cells. At 48 hours, mean killing is 80 per cent for P with D, 55 per cent for P without D and 50 per cent for the matched CAR-X cells lacking R with or without D. Antigen-X-knockout targets and unengineered T cells with D give five per cent. The matched comparisons support an R/D-associated contribution in this donor’s assay, while the knockout and D controls test alternatives. Three wells are technical replicates from one donor, not three donors; no uncertainty interval is supplied. Tumour entry, general benefit and human safety remain different questions.

The fictional healthy-epithelial-organoid card measures survival at 48 hours with D in both arms: 90 per cent with P-generated T cells and 95 per cent with matched CAR-X cells lacking R. There are two organoid donors and one T-cell donor. The five-percentage-point difference needs uncertainty and an interpretation of harm; no acceptable threshold is supplied. It neither tests every healthy tissue nor defines a clinical safety window. Expression, binding, cell injury in culture and organ injury in people are different observations.

The fictional mouse card compares administered carrier P with empty carrier, with D in both arms and six mice per arm. One selected day-seven blood sample has 120 dual-positive cells among 200 T cells, or 60 per cent; this is not the six-mouse denominator, and two treated biopsies contain few engineered cells. Mean tumour volume is stated as 100 cubic millimetres at baseline, then 300 for P and 1,000 for control at day 28. P is 70 per cent smaller than control but three times the stated baseline: reduced growth, not regression below baseline or cure. Later follow-up, spread and causes of poor entry are missing. Without a matched CAR-X-without-R mouse arm, the comparison cannot isolate R’s contribution or establish every animal’s outcome.

Matching the fictional payload identities of lots A, B and C does not transfer lot A’s functional results to B and C. These are three lots, not three independent cell donors; potency and post-storage performance need relevant measurements. Likewise, at 24 hours after D withdrawal the fictional support signal falls from 100 to 20 relative units versus 100 with continued D, an 80 per cent signal reduction, while 90 of 100 tracked cells remain. Those are three technical wells from the same donor. The result does not demonstrate cell elimination, absent CAR recognition or reversal of injury.

The fictional packet contains no human study, so it has no clinical response or adverse-event denominator. An absent dataset is not a zero-per-cent rate, and target cells killed in culture are not people with a study-defined objective response. For each card, state the claim earned, the claim not earned and the next measurement, carrying product, specimen, comparator, donor or participant denominator, time and uncertainty. Do not fill one product’s missing evidence with another’s success. On a logarithmic axis, 100, 1,000 and 10,000 are tenfold steps rather than equal additive changes. Early human activity, comparative benefit and transfer to another product remain distinct evidence levels.

Tuerxunyiming’s 2026 work provides another model-specific example. An engineered Sindbis-envelope lentiviral system delivered a CD19 CAR in NPG mice carrying human blood mononuclear cells and Raji lymphoma. The experiment compared repeated vector administration with infusion of cells engineered in culture, using selected mice with measured human T-cell engraftment. Tumour control and CAR-positive blood fractions were different readouts; the in vivo-generated group had a lower CAR-positive fraction than the infused-cell group. These are human-cell/mouse experiments, not treatment of people or proof of exclusive delivery in every tissue.
records.principle: Deliver encoding instructions into a defined cell population in the body, then measure which cells are engineered, where they go, how long expression lasts and what those cells do.
strengths: Investigates an alternative to administering cells engineered outside the body
May reduce some separate ex vivo manufacturing steps in a specified process
limitations: Cell targeting, off-target engineering and immune responses require measurement
Instruction dose does not specify final cell number or functional exposure
Conditioning, repeat dosing and cost are product- and protocol-specific

records.name: Cell-therapy safety switches
records.tldr: An engineered switch can control a specified cell activity or promote cell removal. Lower signaling, fewer living cells and reversal of injury are different outcomes.
records.summary:
A living cell product can persist after administration stops. Activity switches regulate a defined function; elimination switches aim to remove cells. A drug-gated receptor may require a supplied molecule for signaling, whereas inducible caspase-9 activates a cell-death pathway when its dimerizing trigger is given. A removable surface tag offers another clearance route. These mechanisms need evidence within the actual finished product, including trigger exposure, speed, completeness and residual activity. None guarantees instant removal from every tissue or reversal of prior injury.

Di Stasi tested inducible caspase-9 in donor T cells after haploidentical stem-cell transplantation, rather than as a general CAR-T rescue trial. In the GD2-CART01 neuroblastoma report, the suicide switch was activated in one participant.

Wang et al. 2011, Blood: a transgene-encoded cell surface polypeptide (truncated EGFR) for selection, tracking and ablation of engineered cells
Wu et al.: small-molecule ON-switch CAR experiments (2015)
Del Bufalo et al.: GD2-CART01 neuroblastoma study and activated suicide gene (2023)
FDA: CAR T-cell product-development guidance, including related engineered lymphocytes (2024)
Inducible apoptosis as a safety switch for adoptive cell therapy. (2011)

notes: Wu separated antigen-binding and signaling components in an ON-switch CAR that assembled under a small-molecule input in preclinical systems. Reducing a controlled signal is different from eliminating every cell. Trigger clearance, response time and remaining functions need their own measurements.

In the five-person Di Stasi study, four recipients developed graft-versus-host disease and received AP1903. The report describes a reduction exceeding 90% of modified T cells within half an hour and control of that disease. This is a specified transplant setting, not proof of complete whole-body clearance or reversal of every CAR-associated toxicity.

Wang described a truncated EGFR marker lacking ligand-binding regions and intracellular kinase activity while retaining a cetuximab-binding epitope. The cell-engineering report studied selection, tracking and antibody-mediated clearance. A drug having an approved use does not establish that every marker/antibody combination is a validated clinical rescue system.

The Del Bufalo GD2-CART01 phase 1/2 report states that the inducible caspase-9 suicide gene was activated in one participant, with rapid elimination reported. This observation does not establish the speed or completeness of every other switch.

Record the exact trigger, concentration, time and viable-cell input. Compare switch-positive and switch-negative cells and untriggered controls. Keep receptor signaling, secretion, proliferation, target-cell killing, absolute surviving cells and the surviving fraction distinct. A sequence check does not demonstrate a functional switch. Check baseline leakage, incomplete switch expression, survivors that regrow, and the trigger’s access to relevant tissues. Evaluate the switch after manufacture within the finished cell product; a sequence result cannot substitute for these functional tests.

A fictional activity assay could fall sharply while many viable cells remain and retain target killing. The supported conclusion would be reduced activity in that assay, not complete cell elimination or resolved injury. Sampled blood or a culture well does not establish the result in every tissue.

In a fictional matched blood measurement, 100 modified cells fall to five after a trigger, a 95 per cent reduction. A cytokine readout falls, but organ injury is unchanged. These are three different outcomes: sampled cell abundance, inflammatory signal and injury. Ask whether viable survivors retain receptor function, which tissues were sampled, when the measurements were made and whether survivors regrow. A sequence check or six people observed for four weeks without an event cannot establish a functioning rescue mechanism, complete body-wide clearance, zero risk or reversal of an injury already present. A usable control plan also depends on switch expression, trigger delivery to the relevant cells and access to the drug and specialist care; an encoded switch alone establishes none of these.

The five participants in Di Stasi’s inducible-caspase-9 study were aged three to 17 and had received haploidentical stem-cell transplants. Four developed graft-versus-host disease and received the dimerising drug. The reported rapid fall in modified T cells and control of that disease belong to this donor-cell/transplant setting; they are not a demonstration that the same switch reverses every CAR-associated inflammatory, neurologic or healthy-tissue injury.
records.principle: Name the controlled process and trigger, then measure receptor activity, viable engineered-cell abundance and downstream harms separately before and after triggering.
strengths: Additional control over a specified activity or a cell population in tested constructs
limitations: Some cells or functions can survive the trigger
Released mediators and tissue injury can persist after cells decline
Cell removal can also remove useful activity; trigger access and product quality matter

records.name: Vein-to-vein time and manufacturing slots
records.tldr: The time from collecting a person’s cells to infusing their prepared cell product. It includes transport, testing and clinical readiness as well as manufacture.
records.summary:
Vein-to-vein time is the interval from collection of a person’s cells to infusion of the prepared cell product. Collection, transport, manufacture, testing, release and clinical readiness contribute to that interval; culture time alone does not describe it. The definition, starting event and analysis population should be stated when comparing programmes.

FDA’s 2024 CAR T-cell guidance recommends planning for manufacturing delays or failures, reassessing eligibility before administration and analysing failure to reach treatment as a possible feasibility endpoint. A product that does not meet its release criteria and a person who becomes unable to receive treatment are different events. Neither a generic turnaround estimate nor a cross-trial waiting-time difference by itself establishes why clinical outcomes differ.

notes: Count the pathway as well as the interval. A collection, a completed lot, a lot meeting its requirements and an infusion are different events. In the historical gavo-cel phase-I report, 48 participants underwent apheresis intending treatment, 32 were infused and 30 were response-evaluable. Those denominators describe different stages; the differences cannot all be called manufacturing failure. Delivery formats can change the process, but transport, quality decisions, clinical readiness and access still require evidence for the actual programme.

records.name: Cell-manufacturing outcomes and nonconforming products
records.tldr: Making a cell product, meeting its quality requirements, shipping it and treating a person are different outcomes. A report's definition and denominator determine what its success rate means.
records.summary: A process can stop without a product, produce a nonconforming lot, make a conforming product that is never shipped, or supply material that is never infused. Out-of-specification means at least one stated requirement was missed; it does not determine which attribute, severity or disposition applies. Studies sometimes include such lots within manufacturing failure, while others report separate categories. Keep orders, collections, runs, batches, people, cancellations and follow-up with the reported measure.

Approved, remanufactured, infused and never-infused people remain separate groups. Its report of no statistically significant outcome differences is not a demonstration of equivalence, and its associations do not establish individual risk or treatment selection.

records.name: Apheresis (leukapheresis)
records.tldr: Apheresis separates components from blood and returns other components to the circulation. Leukapheresis collects a white-cell-rich mixture that can be starting material for a cell therapy or research.
records.summary: Leukapheresis uses an extracorporeal separation circuit to collect white-cell-rich material. A leukopak can contain lymphocytes and monocytes in variable proportions; it is not automatically a purified T-cell population or a released treatment. The collection method, intended cells and receiving programme determine the required material, measurements and handling. Collection for a cell therapy, research or a stem-cell procedure retains its own protocol rather than sharing one duration or universal preparation rule.

Citrate anticoagulant can lower available calcium and cause symptoms requiring monitoring or treatment; access, blood-pressure, bleeding and infection risks depend on the procedure and person. The NIH consent example is not a universal duration, risk estimate or permission to change medicines.

Prior treatment, current cell composition, collection and shipping conditions can affect the starting material. Retain source identity, time, handling, receiving acceptance and relevant samples through subsequent manufacture. A successful collection does not guarantee culture growth, a conforming final lot or eventual infusion.

Research collection and therapeutic collection can have different acceptance, consent, banking and testing requirements. Tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte manufacture uses tumour-derived material, not simply this blood collection. Vaccines and other cell-based protocols have their own collection requirements; leukapheresis is not a universal prerequisite for vaccination.

A need for a pretreatment baseline or a specified cell input can make timing important, but the name vaccine supplies no universal requirement to collect blood first. Those different starting materials do not establish a common collection order or validate giving resulting treatments together.

records.name: Allogeneic (off-the-shelf) cell therapy
records.tldr: Allogeneic cell therapy uses cells from someone other than the recipient. A banked product may avoid collecting the recipient's cells, but treatment still requires a suitable product and clinical preparation.
records.summary: Autologous cells come from the intended recipient; allogeneic cells come from another person. This source distinction is separate from whether engineering occurs outside or inside the body and from whether a cell product or a carrier is administered. Donor-cell manufacture can provide inventory for later recipients, but usable supply, quality disposition, matching requirements, preparation and clinical eligibility still govern access. Donor immune cells can attack recipient tissues, while the recipient's immune system can reject donor cells. The relevant mechanisms depend on cell type, construct, edits, conditioning and setting.

records.name: Lymphodepletion before CAR-T
records.tldr: A short course of chemotherapy (usually fludarabine and cyclophosphamide) given in the days before a CAR-T infusion to clear out the patient's own lymphocytes, making room and growth signals for the engineered cells to expand.
records.summary: Lymphodepletion removes regulatory T cells and cytokine sinks, raising IL-7 and IL-15 levels so infused CAR-T cells proliferate; its intensity correlates with expansion, response and also toxicity. Fludarabine shortages led to bendamustine substitution with similar outcomes. It causes a week or two of cytopenias and infection risk and contributes to prolonged cytopenias after CAR-T. In vivo CAR-T approaches and some allogeneic products aim to work without lymphodepletion, which would remove a major barrier to outpatient and community delivery. Vein-to-vein time includes the wait for manufacturing before lymphodepletion can begin.

notes: Why preparing the body can help transferred cells, and what it costs. In mouse adoptive-transfer experiments, a nonmyeloablative regimen enhanced antitumour effect even without regulatory T cells, through greater function of tumour-reactive CD8-positive T cells rather than greater numbers; interleukin-7 and interleukin-15 were required, and removing endogenous cells that respond to those cytokines reproduced the effect, which points to lymphodepletion removing cells that act as cytokine sinks (Gattinoni et al.). That is a mouse mechanism and it does not describe an empty physical space. When a trial tests conditioning, transferred cells and cytokine support together, the outcomes belong to the whole package: in the phase 3 tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte trial in advanced melanoma (Rohaan et al.; 168 patients, 86 per cent with disease refractory to anti-PD-1 treatment), cells were infused after nonmyeloablative cyclophosphamide plus fludarabine and followed by high-dose interleukin-2, and grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in all patients given TILs, mainly chemotherapy-related myelosuppression. Nonmyeloablative therefore does not mean harmless.

Counts need their denominators. A percentage of white cells is not an absolute count: with invented numbers, 20 per cent of 2,000 white cells per microlitre is 400 lymphocytes, and a later 40 per cent of 500 is 200, so the fraction doubled while the count halved. Lymphocyte and neutrophil counts are separate measurements, cytopenia means a low count of any blood cell type, and none of these measures tumour killing.

Lymphocytes include T cells, B cells and natural killer cells. Preparation can affect competition, regulation and, for donor products, host rejection; it can also act on cancer directly. It does not create a missing tumour antigen or guarantee that transferred cells enter a solid tumour. The need for preparation and its recovery criteria belong to the named protocol, rather than to every cell therapy. Serial blood counts consume blood samples rather than tumour tissue. Report absolute lymphocytes and neutrophils with units, sampling time and reference ranges, and measure transferred-cell number, location and function separately from the counts. More depletion is not automatically more benefit. Nonmyeloablative describes a regimen not intended to eliminate marrow blood production completely, rather than a promise of mild count suppression. Report severity, duration, recovery, infections, organ harms and relevant support with the regimen. More transferred cells, more depletion and more tumour killing are separate propositions.

records.name: On-target, off-tumour toxicity and off-target cross-reactivity
records.tldr: On-target, off-tumour toxicity is harm to healthy tissue that carries the same target a treatment was built to recognise, so accurate recognition injures the tissue as well as the cancer.
records.summary:
On-target, off-tumour toxicity is injury from recognition of the intended target on healthy tissue. It differs from recognition of an unintended molecular target. The predictable, lymphoma-specific consequences of aiming at lineage antigens (B-cell aplasia, low immunoglobulin, and the effects of CD52, CCR4 and CD47 targeting) are described in the record on the cost of aiming at a lineage antigen, which this record does not repeat.

Many candidate cancer targets are normal proteins found at different levels or places in the body, so tumour-associated does not mean tumour-exclusive. A treatment that recognises its intended target wherever it is accessible, such as a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell, can harm any healthy tissue that displays it, and tissue location, target density, receptor properties and exposure all shape the outcome. This differs from off-target cross-reactivity, in which the receptor recognises an unintended molecule, and from cytokine release syndrome, which is systemic inflammatory activation; the three can occur together. It also differs from payload toxicity in an antibody-drug conjugate: a pooled analysis of ADC trials found the key grade 3 to 4 toxicities grouped by payload and concluded they were likely off-target and related to the payload (Masters et al., 2018). Binding specificity is not tissue selectivity, and experience with an antibody against a target does not automatically carry over to a living cell with a different recognition and signalling system.

Two primary reports show the contrast. A patient with colon cancer metastatic to the lungs and liver received 10 billion autologous T cells expressing a trastuzumab-based CAR against ERBB2 (HER2), the largest number permitted in the first dose-escalation cohort, the day after a lymphodepleting regimen of cyclophosphamide (60 mg/kg daily for 2 days) and fludarabine (25 mg/m2 for 5 days). Within 15 minutes the patient had respiratory distress, chest imaging showed pulmonary oedema, and the patient died 5 days after treatment, with marked rises in interferon-gamma, GM-CSF, tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10. At autopsy multiple organs showed systemic ischaemia and haemorrhagic microangiopathic injury and the lungs diffuse alveolar damage; histological examination of autopsy tissue found ERBB2 at 3+ in liver metastases and 2+ in lung metastases and much lower levels in normal lung parenchyma, normal liver and normal breast. The authors hypothesised that highly active ERBB2-directed T cells recognised ERBB2 on normal lung cells on first pass through the lung and released inflammatory cytokines that began a cascade ending in multiorgan failure; the autopsy findings were read as initial lung injury followed by days of hypotension and ischaemia, and the authors call the significance of the cells' reactivity against cultured primary cells unclear. This is a single case, with a stated dose and conditioning, whose mechanism is the authors' hypothesis and which gives no incidence for any CAR product (Morgan et al., 2010). In a trial of an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor against HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 in myeloma and melanoma, the first two patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days; no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and beating cardiomyocytes made from induced pluripotent stem cells triggered T-cell killing through recognition of an unrelated peptide from titin. That is off-target recognition of an unintended molecule, not the intended target in the wrong tissue (Linette et al., 2013).

How the question is asked before and during trials. FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. In practice a readout is a staining intensity or positive fraction, a binding profile, killing or cytokine release by healthy cells at a named time, and finally organ injury in the treated population; stained fixed tissue does not show a living organ's accessibility, an animal model may lack the human target, and a negative result in one panel is not a safety certificate. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

If it also recognises Y on an X-negative healthy cell, that is off-target cross-reactivity. Binding or surface contact does not itself measure injury. Record tissue, assay sensitivity, staining intensity, positive fraction or calibrated molecules per cell, binding specificity, and healthy-cell killing or cytokine release at a named time; viable-cell tests consume the sample. Clinical organ injury is a further outcome in the actual population and regimen. A staining ratio, one negative panel or a control switch does not establish safety everywhere or guarantee reversal of an injury already present.

In a fictional tumour sample, 70 of 100 cells display an epitope accessible to the proposed receptor and 30 do not. A second target has only an RNA result, while healthy tissue was stained with a third antibody. Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. A sampled panel can miss antigen-negative cells, and an intracellular signal does not establish an accessible surface epitope. Repeat the relevant healthy-cell question under conditions, including inflammation, that could change recognition.

records.name: TROP2
records.tldr: TROP2 is a surface protein found in normal epithelial cells and many cancers. It is used to deliver antibody-drug conjugates and has biological signalling roles; those observations do not establish an individual tumour’s response.
records.summary: TROP2, encoded by TACSTD2, is a transmembrane protein used as a delivery target by sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan. Experimental studies have also linked wild-type TROP2 expression and signalling to growth in defined cell and animal models. Its delivery role, biological function, possible genomic alterations and clinical treatment-selection rules are separate questions. The current U.S. breast-cancer indications of these two ADCs do not require a TROP2 expression test, while other disease, prior-treatment and regimen-specific criteria still apply.

The ungated construct caused lung injury and inflammation in that model. records.name: CAR-T cell therapy
records.tldr: CAR-T therapy uses T cells carrying an engineered receptor. Approved products treat selected blood cancers, with product-specific eligibility and safety requirements.
records.summary:
CAR-T cell therapy uses T cells carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize a target. FDA-approved products include CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T cells for selected blood cancers, including B-cell leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma. The individual product label defines the treatment setting and eligibility. A common autologous approach collects a person’s T cells, engineers and expands them outside the body, then infuses them back; conditioning and follow-up depend on the protocol.

A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

In early work, Gross, Waks and Eshhar joined antibody-variable regions to T-cell receptor components in 1989. Eshhar and colleagues subsequently tested single-chain antibody-binding regions joined to gamma or zeta signaling chains in 1993. These experimental designs helped separate recognition from the signaling machinery attached to it.

FDA-approved examples include tisagenlecleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, obecabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel. Their labeled diseases, treatment settings and eligibility differ; the individual product records retain those distinctions.

notes: Generation labels describe common signaling architectures. First-generation constructs use an activation domain, often CD3 zeta; second-generation designs add one costimulatory region; third-generation designs combine two. Fourth-generation and later labels vary across authors. More domains do not establish better patient outcomes. The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.

CD28 and 4-1BB are borrowed intracellular signaling regions, not separately administered receptors. Kawalekar compared metabolic and memory features in defined human-cell experiments. Ramos co-infused two specified second- and third-generation products in lymphoma; different expansion and persistence did not isolate comparative clinical benefit. Neither study ranks all products by signaling-domain name.

Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts. Compare otherwise matched constructs, target-positive and target-negative cells, healthy-tissue targets and unstimulated activity. Hudecek found that particular IgG-derived spacers could support killing in a dish yet impair activity in mouse models through Fc interactions.

A peptide-HLA target is an exception to blanket HLA-independent descriptions. Rafiq tested a WT1 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 in cell and mouse models; this was a proof of concept, not evidence that every intracellular protein or every HLA type is addressable by that construct.

A 2024 preprint used a pooled signaling-domain library, repeated stimulation and single-cell sequencing to study how domain arrangement affected T-cell states over time. Its membrane-proximal-domain findings are construct-and-assay observations, not a clinical ranking of domains or a validation of pooled-screen hits as treatments.

FDA initiated boxed-warning changes in 2024 for the risk of T-cell malignancies after the then-approved BCMA- or CD19-directed autologous CAR T-cell products. Its communication calls for lifelong monitoring for secondary malignancies. This is a scoped regulatory warning, not a claim that every type of engineered immune cell has the same risk.

In June 2025, FDA eliminated REMS requirements for the named autologous CAR T-cell products in its notice. Product warnings and safety monitoring continued. The manufacturer postmarketing observational studies with 15-year follow-up described in that notice are different from the lifelong patient-monitoring statement in the earlier safety communication.

A receptor-bearing cell, its genetic instructions and its receptor protein are different objects. For a protein-coding instruction, DNA is transcribed into RNA, and a ribosome translates usable messenger RNA into protein. Delivered messenger RNA starts at the translation step. Folding and transport to the membrane still have to occur before a surface receptor can bind its target. In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.

Kymriah’s product description illustrates why borrowed parts do not identify the whole product. Its CD19-binding region is a murine-derived single-chain antibody fragment, followed by a CD8-derived hinge and transmembrane region and the internal 4-1BB/CD137 and CD3-zeta signalling domains. CD8 here names the origin of structural segments, not a claim that the infused preparation contains only CD8 T cells. The label describes enrichment for T cells and permits other cell populations. Autologous source, domain names and architecture do not transfer Kymriah’s clinical results to another construct.

Suppose two fictional CARs differ only in their hinge: both bind purified antigen, but only one kills antigen-bearing cells. Compare surface expression and the geometry of cell contact before concluding that affinity is the problem. Likewise, DNA-positive cells without killing leave RNA production, receptor folding and trafficking, actual binding and signalling as separate possible failure points. Hudecek’s R11 ROR1 experiments illustrate a product-specific constraint: a long spacer enabled recognition of its membrane-proximal epitope, while changes that reduced Fc-receptor binding improved activity in the tested mice. Longer is not a universal design rule. Treat the transmembrane segment as part of the finished construct: assess assembly, surface expression and interactions rather than presume it is a neutral anchor. Unstimulated signalling and responses to repeated target encounters also need separate assessment.

In a fictional population of 100 cancer cells, 80 display target X and 20 do not. Killing the X-positive 80 leaves 20 survivors; ten times as many effector cells does not create X on them. For two targets, suppose 20 cells carry both X and Y, 60 carry X only, ten Y only and ten neither. An idealised either-target rule covers 90 cells, whereas a both-target rule covers 20. These are recognition-coverage calculations, not measured killing or healthy-tissue selectivity. Expression thresholds, tissue access and cell function still matter.

TNBC describes a breast-cancer subtype, not one universal receptor target. A research programme, a positive stain or a named cell platform does not establish a treatment indication or rank safe recognition strategies. The cited TROP2 work supplies preclinical observations, and the ROR1 phase-I report supplies limited activity and infiltration observations in its actual mixed population. These studies do not supply a comparative clinical-benefit estimate for every antigen-directed product in TNBC. Individual labels and clinical studies define their own disease, regimen and eligibility scope.

Kawalekar’s defined human-CAR experiments linked 4-1BB signalling to outgrowth of CD8 central-memory cells with greater respiratory capacity, fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis. CD28-containing CARs produced effector-memory cells with a gene-expression pattern consistent with greater glycolysis. These are construct-and-system observations, not a ranking of clinical speed, persistence or safety by domain name. Other receptor parts, preparation, starting-cell state, target and disease setting remain relevant. Ramos simultaneously infused separately tracked second- and third-generation products. Their different expansion and persistence did not let a shared tumour response isolate either product’s clinical contribution.

Relapse mechanisms need separate investigation. Sotillo found CD19 sequence and splicing changes affecting recognition in B-ALL relapse material and experiments. Deng found infusion-product transcriptional features associated with outcomes in a selected cohort of 24 large B-cell lymphoma infusion products; those associations did not prove that one engineered modification would correct every failure.
records.principle: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region. Conventional surface-antigen recognition can bypass peptide-HLA presentation; specialized peptide-HLA-targeting CARs retain the relevant HLA and antigen-processing requirements.

limitations: Shared healthy-tissue targets and inflammatory, neurologic or blood-count harms
Manufacturing, access and cost depend on the product and setting

records.name: B7-H3
records.tldr: B7-H3 is an immune checkpoint-like surface protein found on 60 to 70% of small-cell lung cancers and 80 to 90% of castration-resistant prostate cancers, with little on normal tissue. It is used as an ADC address, chiefly by ifinatamab deruxtecan, now in phase 3 in small-cell lung cancer; whether blocking its immune-dampening role adds anything beyond payload delivery is unresolved.
records.summary: B7-H3 (CD276) is an immune checkpoint-like molecule broadly overexpressed in solid tumours with limited normal expression; its function is debated, inhibiting T-cell activation and promoting tumour cell migration. Expression is more homogeneous than many ADC targets, found in 60-70% of small-cell lung cancer and 80-90% of castration-resistant prostate cancer by IHC, as well as head and neck and paediatric solid tumours. Ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) has shown high response rates in small-cell lung cancer and is in phase 3. B7-H3 is also pursued with radioligands and CAR-T. Whether its immune-dampening role means antibodies against it add an immunological benefit beyond payload delivery is unresolved. The simple version is a widely present tumour surface protein now used mainly as an address for ADCs.

records.name: MUC1 (mucin-1)

records.summary:

records.name: EGFR
records.tldr: A growth receptor that is mutated in some lung cancers and overproduced in others; the first great success of targeted pills.
records.summary: EGFR activating mutations (exon 19 del, L858R) drive ~15% of Western and ~40-50% of East Asian NSCLC; osimertinib is standard first-line. EGFR is also an antibody target in colorectal and head-and-neck cancer (cetuximab, panitumumab) and a component of bispecifics (amivantamab, EGFR×MET; EGFR×HER3 ADCs). Resistance via C797S, MET amplification, and histologic transformation is the central problem.

notes: EGFR, also called HER1 or ERBB1, is a receptor tyrosine kinase. Ligand binding outside the cell can change receptor arrangement and the activity of phosphate-transfer machinery inside. Cetuximab binds the extracellular region, whereas an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor acts at the intracellular kinase. An antibody conjugate instead adds a cargo-delivery job to target recognition. Its mechanism and evidence need separate assessment, including any antibody-mediated immune effects. A schematic contact or cargo arrow is not a molecular map of receptor processing, and delivery to a recognised target does not by itself establish dependence on the receptor kinase.

EGFR can feed RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT signalling, but these networks receive other inputs too. A downstream signal therefore does not uniquely identify the receptor driving it. Compare the actual inhibitor: which receptors and variants it covers, whether binding is reversible and what exposure is achieved. Evidence for an extracellular antibody cannot simply be assigned to an intracellular kinase inhibitor, even when both treatments use the same target name.

Lynch and colleagues linked defined EGFR kinase-domain mutations to gefitinib responsiveness in non-small-cell lung cancer and tested the mutant proteins in cultured cells. They found mutations in eight of nine responsive cancers and none of seven nonresponsive cancers in the reported comparison. This was evidence about specific alterations in that disease and about their functional consequences, not a rule that abundant EGFR protein in another cancer predicts response.

TBCRC 001 studied cetuximab with carboplatin in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Among 16 patients with paired biopsies, the expression-based EGFR pathway analysis showed activation in 13 and inhibition after treatment in five. The regimen given together from the start produced a 17% response rate; 31% had a response or prolonged disease stabilisation. The latter outcome is broader than objective response. Receptor abundance, measured pathway suppression and clinical disease control cannot be substituted for each other.

BALI-1 compared cisplatin with or without cetuximab in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Its primary overall-response endpoint was not met: response was 20% versus 10%, with P = 0.11. Progression-free survival was a secondary endpoint, and the reported overall-survival difference was not statistically significant. These results do not establish a general EGFR-treatment rule or postoperative benefit. The later erratum added a funding acknowledgement rather than changing these efficacy results.

An EGFR report identifies the specimen, assay, variant if any and sampling time. Immunostaining measures protein amount and location; sequencing measures a DNA alteration; receptor or downstream phosphorylation measures a particular signalling state. A staining score, variant allele fraction and signal normalised to a control have different denominators and units. In model tests, state concentration and controls and distinguish engagement from growth dependence. An unspecified EGFR-high cutoff cannot select every EGFR-directed medicine.

In a fictional culture with strong EGFR staining, reduced receptor phosphorylation after treatment and continued growth, the stain and phosphoprotein result can both be correct. Growth may have other support, and attribution to the intended target still needs controlled perturbation and comparable exposure. This pattern does not establish sensitivity or patient benefit. Explain separately how much receptor was observed, what the exact alteration does and which product-specific mechanism and clinical outcome have been demonstrated.

A total-EGFR measurement does not specify recognition by an EGFR806 CAR. Subham’s study used an mAb806-derived binding region in a particular construct and examined TNBC brain-metastasis tissue, cell lines and mice. Its antibody-derived spacer was modified to reduce Fc-receptor recognition. Statements about tumour-restricted binding or normal-brain expression in the introduction draw on earlier work; they are not a substitute for testing the proposed finished receptor against relevant healthy cells. This preclinical result is not a clinical breast-cancer benefit or safety estimate.

Triple-negative breast cancer: EGFR is amplified or gained in 23% of basal-like tumours but rarely mutated (Cancer Genome Atlas 2012), high-level amplification 3 to 6% by cohort (cBioPortal); EGFR-directed antibodies failed unselected, and the receptor now matters as one arm of the EGFR-HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate izalontamab brengitecan.

Colorectal cancer: a target without an alteration. Cetuximab and panitumumab work in RAS and BRAF wild-type, left-sided disease regardless of EGFR copy number or expression, and no EGFR test selects them; the biomarkers are negative ones (Karapetis 2008, Douillard 2013) plus primary tumour side (Arnold 2017). High-level EGFR amplification is 1 to 2% (cBioPortal) and epiregulin overexpression marks the distal, ligand-dependent tumours (Missiaglia 2014). Acquired resistance is read in plasma as emerging KRAS, NRAS, BRAF and EGFR ectodomain alterations, detectable months before imaging (Misale 2012, Diaz 2012).

Lung cancer: mutated in 12.4% of resected Western adenocarcinoma and 47.4% of East Asian adenocarcinoma, with 28.4% in never-smoker whole genomes (cBioPortal), the widest ancestry gap of any biomarker in solid-tumour oncology. The mutation classes differ: exon 19 deletions (about 14% of adenocarcinomas), L858R (about 11%), exon 20 insertions (about 2%) and the uncommon G719X, L861Q and S768I variants need drug-specific evidence. Response to every generation, or resistance to every inhibitor, does not follow from the class name. In July 2025, the FDA granted accelerated approval to sunvozertinib for adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer with an EGFR exon 20 insertion detected by an FDA-approved test after progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. Resistance is read in the same gene: T790M in 63% of rebiopsies after a first-generation inhibitor (Yu 2013) and C797S in 22% after osimertinib, where the allelic phase with T790M decides whether a combination can cover it (Thress 2015, Oxnard 2018). Immunohistochemistry measures protein rather than identifying these DNA alterations.

records.name: ROR1
records.tldr: ROR1 is a fetal pseudo-kinase receptor re-expressed on over 90% of chronic lymphocytic leukaemias, 30 to 50% of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas and 40 to 60% of triple-negative breast cancers, and largely absent from healthy adult tissue. records.summary: ROR1 is an oncofetal receptor tyrosine kinase-like protein, a Wnt5a pseudo-kinase receptor that drives survival signalling in CLL and mantle cell lymphoma and is largely absent from normal adult tissue. Surface expression is seen in over 90% of CLL, 30-50% of DLBCL, and 40-60% of TNBC by IHC, with NSCLC expression also reported. Zilovertamab vedotin (MK-2140), an ADC, is in phase 3 in DLBCL, and the TNBC and NSCLC expression supports solid-tumour programmes. Because the receptor is a pseudo-kinase, it is used as a delivery address rather than a signalling target, and whether expression level predicts ADC benefit remains to be shown. The simple version is an embryonic receptor that many cancers re-express, giving ADCs a target largely missing from healthy cells.

records.tldr: Tissue factor is a clotting protein that cancers abnormally display on their surface, used as an ADC target in cervical cancer.
records.summary: Tissue factor (F3) initiates the extrinsic coagulation cascade; when cancers display it abnormally on their surface it drives thrombosis and angiogenesis, and it becomes an ADC target. It is overexpressed in cervical, pancreatic, head and neck, and ovarian tumours, with 90-95% of cervical and 50-80% of pancreatic cancers positive by IHC. Tisotumab vedotin (Tivdak) is approved in recurrent cervical cancer on the basis of innovaTV 301, and innovaTV did not select patients on tissue factor expression, so the drug is given without a companion test. Topoisomerase-I payload successors (XNW28012) are in phase 3. The open questions are ocular toxicity management and whether newer payloads widen the indication. The simple version is a clotting protein that cancers wear on their surface, letting an ADC find them.

records.name: Logic-gated therapeutics (AND, NOT gates)
records.tldr: Recognition circuits combine inputs to broaden target coverage or restrict activation. AND-like, OR-like, inhibitory and sequential designs have different failure modes and need direct testing.
records.summary: In cell-based examples, split and tuned activation/costimulation can implement an AND-like requirement, either-target recognition can broaden coverage with an OR-like rule, and a protective-antigen input can inhibit activity. SynNotch-to-CAR systems induce a second receptor over time, creating a primed state rather than requiring two antigens to remain simultaneously present on one cell. Thresholds, expression, decay and movement between tissues matter. An intended rule is a design hypothesis, not proof that healthy tissue is spared or that the complete product improves outcomes.

Activation, proliferation and completed killing are different outputs. That result supports checking preparation and recovery; it does not validate a universal clinical viability cutoff or guarantee freedom from antigen escape.

records.name: TCR-T cell therapy
records.tldr: TCR-T supplies living T cells carrying a selected receptor that recognizes a specified peptide with its presenting HLA molecule. A source-protein name alone does not establish that target.
records.summary:
Conventional alpha-beta TCR-T introduces selected paired receptor-chain instructions into therapeutic T cells. The receptor recognizes a displayed peptide-HLA complex, rather than entering the tumor cell to bind the whole source protein. Natural processing, the required HLA allele, surface display, receptor expression and useful cell function remain different questions. This differs from administering a soluble TCR/CD3 protein that recruits other T cells.

Afamitresgene autoleucel (Tecelra) is an approved TCR-T example. FDA initially approved it in 2024 and converted the specified adult use to traditional approval in June 2026, extending the indication to patients aged 12 and older. Its synovial-sarcoma indication retains prior-chemotherapy, selected HLA and MAGE-A4 testing requirements. The full label also contains exclusions and safety requirements; a broad HLA-A*02 label is not a complete eligibility rule.

Introducing selected recognition instructions differs from expanding a tumor-derived population with its existing receptors. Viral transduction describes a delivery method, not the definition of every receptor-engineering process.

The conventional receptor uses paired alpha and beta chains alongside the CD3 complex. Cloning selected receptor coding sequences means copying instructions; one sequenced chain does not establish a complete functional receptor or its specificity. Expression and assembly in the finished cells require evaluation. The Dong structural study distinguishes recognition chains from associated signaling components. Bendle showed in mouse models that introduced and endogenous chains could form self-reactive mixed receptors; vector and cell-population changes reduced that model risk. This does not supply a clinical risk rate for every TCR-T product.

Protein expression and HLA typing lie upstream of the displayed ligand. Antigen/HLA loss or impaired presentation can remove one recognition route; retaining another allele does not rescue a receptor requiring the lost allele. A different receptor using a retained allele needs its own specificity and functional evidence.

In research, test paired receptor expression and naturally presenting targets, with relevant antigen/HLA removal and restoration, irrelevant peptides, unmodified effectors and healthy tissue. Multimer or peptide-loaded reagent binding is different from natural processing, target-cell death or patient benefit. This research validation is distinct from the approved product’s clinical testing rule.

Cameron investigated fatal cardiac toxicity with one affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 receptor and identified a cross-reactive Titin peptide presented by HLA-A*01 as the most likely cause. Earlier screening had not detected the hazard. This was a different receptor from the MAGE-A4 product Tecelra; stronger binding does not establish improved specificity or safety for either a new construct or an entire family.

The June 2026 Tecelra label names HLA-A*02:01P, -A*02:02P, -A*02:03P and -A*02:06P and a MAGE-A4 tumor test in its indication, with a separate HLA-A*02:05P contraindication. The approval letter documents the adult conversion and pediatric expansion. These are product-specific regulatory scopes, not a general rule for every TCR-T.

Conventional surface-antigen CARs and peptide-HLA-directed receptors have different recognition requirements, but peptide-HLA CARs also exist. The WT1/HLA-A*24:02 CAR study is a preclinical counterexample to saying all intracellular source antigens are unreachable by any CAR. A format change does not supply a missing required peptide-HLA complex.

For a soluble TCR/CD3 protein, the dosed molecule supplies recognition and recruits available T cells. TCR-T instead supplies receptor-bearing living cells. Protein exposure, cell trafficking/persistence and useful target-dependent function need separate measurements; neither format wins by definition.

In a fictional target cell, HLA allele A is lost while B remains. An A-restricted receptor loses that route; a B-restricted receptor still needs its own peptide to be processed and displayed. B2M is the shared light chain for many class-I complexes, whereas class-II HLA uses different alpha and beta chains. Neither one lost allele nor a change in interferon-induced display establishes complete loss of baseline presentation. Test the required allele, antigen and display conditions with matched viable targets rather than infer recognition from the HLA label. A conventional surface-antigen CAR has another dependency, and reduced class I alone does not guarantee NK-cell killing.
records.principle: Selected alpha-beta recognition chains operate with the cell’s CD3 signaling machinery. The intended target is the particular naturally displayed peptide-HLA complex, not genotype, RNA abundance or source protein alone.
strengths: Can investigate targets derived from intracellular proteins through peptide-HLA display

limitations: Allele and antigen-processing/display dependencies can limit recognition

records.name: Central dogma and molecular information flow
records.tldr: DNA copying, making RNA and making a protein are different processes. Following the route helps identify what each molecular test actually measured.
records.summary: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.
