notes: Simoni studied human lung and colorectal tumor infiltrates and found CD8 T cells recognizing viral epitopes unrelated to the cancer. Tumor location did not establish tumor specificity. Its CD39 observations belong to those sampled populations, not a universal marker rule that proves the specificity of every manufactured cell.

Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognize peptide-HLA targets. A mixed TIL product can contain multiple specificities, but breadth must be tested against relevant naturally presenting targets and lesions. Polyclonality does not guarantee freedom from antigen/presentation escape or other resistance.

Record input tissue, culture/selection conditions, viable-cell yield, identity and the final receptor mixture. An expanding bystander clone can increase total yield while reducing the proportion with useful tumor recognition. A receptor repertoire measured before culture is not automatically the infusion product’s repertoire.

A pathology infiltration estimate describes a tissue feature under a specified scoring rule; it is not the viable-cell count recovered for manufacture, a dose, or proof of tumor reactivity. Functional studies need target material, HLA/antigen controls, suitable effectors, timing, units and readout context. Binding, target death and clinical outcome remain different endpoints.

Rohaan randomized patients with advanced melanoma to a specified TIL regimen or ipilimumab. In the reported intention-to-treat population, median progression-free survival was 7.2 versus 3.1 months. The TIL arm included lymphodepleting chemotherapy and high-dose IL-2; grade 3 or higher events in that arm were mainly chemotherapy-related myelosuppression. This comparison concerns the whole regimen and is not the lifileucel registration dataset or an isolated test of cells alone.

FDA’s Amtagvi source describes an autologous tumor-derived product and a defined previously treated melanoma use. The label requires conditioning and post-infusion IL-2 and carries serious regimen warnings. A manufacturing success, a registry listing or a positive cellular assay is not an independent clinical-benefit claim for another process or cancer. Its label lists the specific mechanism of action as unknown. General TIL recognition biology does not establish which clones or components explain an individual response.

The NCT05727904 registry identifies TILVANCE-301 as a randomized phase 3 study in untreated advanced melanoma, with a lifileucel/conditioning/IL-2 regimen plus pembrolizumab compared with pembrolizumab. The registry description does not supply an efficacy result or local availability for a participant.

TIL describes tissue origin, while added receptor or other genetic engineering describes an additional property. Experimental engineering can overlap that origin category; neither name implies the other. Tumor entry before collection also does not guarantee trafficking or useful persistence after transfer.
records.principle: Recover tumor-derived lymphocytes, expand or select them through a specified process, characterize the final cells and evaluate the complete treatment regimen in its disease setting.
strengths: Can investigate multiple naturally occurring recognition specificities
Clinical evidence exists for specified melanoma products and regimens
limitations: Usable tissue and suitable manufacture are required
Bystander cells and culture selection can limit useful recognition
Conditioning, cytokine support, cell infusion and follow-up have their own risks and access requirements

records.name: Natural killer T (NKT) cells
records.tldr: Natural killer T cells are T cells, not a cross between two cell types, and their receptors recognise fat-based molecules shown on a protein called CD1d rather than the protein fragments shown on HLA. Despite the similar name they are a different family from natural killer cells.
records.summary: NKT cells carry a rearranged T-cell receptor, and some also carry receptors usually associated with natural killer cells, but an NK-associated surface marker does not define the family. A review describes their semi-invariant alpha-beta T-cell receptors as recognising CD1d-presented glycolipids, including a mammalian glycosphingolipid and microbial glycuronylceramides (Bendelac et al., 2007). CD1d displays lipid and glycolipid antigens, and the crystal structure of human CD1d with the synthetic glycolipid alpha-galactosylceramide showed the lipid tails fitting inside the groove (Koch et al., 2005). In mouse experiments, Valpha14 NKT cells were activated by a defined glycosylceramide in a CD1d-dependent, receptor-mediated way (Kawano et al., 1997). Type I, or invariant, NKT cells use a strongly shared alpha-chain arrangement with variable beta-chain junctions, found in mouse (Valpha14-Jalpha281) and in a homologous human form (Valpha24-JQ) (Lantz and Bendelac, 1994). Type II NKT cells are more diverse: in mice lacking class II presentation, CD4 T cells with a diverse receptor repertoire included a subset that recognised CD1 (Cardell et al., 1995). 'Invariant' does not mean every chain or every function is identical.

notes: Function depends on the subset and the stimulus. In fresh human blood, lipid-loaded CD1d tetramers separated two subsets of CD1d-restricted T cells that differed in cytokine production and cytotoxic activation, and antigenic stimulation induced cytokines but not perforin whereas inflammatory factors enhanced perforin (Gumperz et al., 2002). In mouse sarcoma and melanoma-metastasis models, tumour rejection was a specialised function of liver-derived NKT cells and mainly of the CD4-negative fraction, while thymus-derived NKT cells were impaired, in part through interleukin-4 production (Crowe et al., 2005). So 'NKT' alone cannot mean protection against cancer, even within one species. An engineered receptor is a separate recognition route: CAR-NKT, CAR-NK and CAR-T are different cell families, and native and engineered recognition have to be measured separately. A phase 1 trial reported interim results for autologous NKT cells engineered to express a GD2-specific CAR with interleukin-15 in three children with neuroblastoma (NCT03294954): no dose-limiting toxicities were observed and one patient had an objective response (Heczey et al., 2020). Separate trials illustrate the other two families: an anti-CD19 CAR-NK product made from cord blood was given to 11 patients with relapsed or refractory CD19-positive cancers in a phase 1 and 2 trial (Liu et al., 2020), and tisagenlecleucel, an anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy, was given to 75 evaluable children and young adults in a phase 2 study in which the overall remission rate within 3 months was 81 per cent (Maude et al., 2018). Those trials concern other cells, diseases and products and say nothing about NKT cells.

A tetramer loaded with a defined CD1d antigen identifies the cells that bind that complex, so a negative result does not count cells with other specificities, and a gate of NK-marker-positive T cells (sometimes called NKT-like) needs its operational definition stated. Counting such cells does not establish tumour killing, and a change in classical HLA display does not show that CD1d, its antigen or an effective NKT response is present.

An NK-associated marker is insufficient to define an NKT cell. Benlagha et al. (2000) identified glycolipid-reactive T cells with CD1d1-alpha-galactosylceramide tetramers, including an NK1.1-negative population in mice, while natural killer cells did not bind those tetramers. This is a studied glycolipid-reactive subset, not a universal detection test for all type II NKT cells. NKT cells can carry NK-associated receptors, but a marker-positive T-cell gate and a defined CD1d-reactive T-cell population are different operational definitions.

records.name: T cell
records.tldr: T cells are immune cells with different recognition systems and roles. Their presence does not by itself show that they recognise or kill cancer.
records.summary: T cells develop through the thymus. Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognise peptide-HLA displays through a paired receptor; CD4 and CD8 identify major co-receptor populations, rather than fixed helper and killer jobs. Some human bladder-tumour CD4 cells showed class-II-dependent cytotoxicity in controlled experiments, while regulatory populations restrain responses. Identity, receptor specificity, state and measured function need separate evidence. A CD3 or CD8 stain establishes a sampled population under a defined panel, not tumour recognition or killing. Report compartment, viable-cell denominator, marker panel and timing. Controlled recognition and target-cell-death assays address different claims; cytokine production, division and treatment benefit are also separate outcomes.

notes: T cells are a lymphocyte family, not every white cell or every lymphocyte. Precursors develop through the thymus, with receptor generation and selection shaping the peripheral pool. Conventional alpha-beta cells recognise peptide-HLA; gamma-delta cells use another, context-dependent receptor system, so conventional peptide-HLA examples do not describe every T cell.

T-cell descriptions should separate identity, location, specificity, state and measured function. Flow cytometry uses defined viable-cell gates and panels, tissue staining adds location and sequencing adds receptor identity. Report compartment, denominator, panel and timing. CD3/CD8 positivity and a viral-peptide response establish their tested observations, not cancer recognition or killing by every nearby cell; greater presence or activation does not automatically mean clinical benefit.

records.name: Batch release (lot disposition)
records.tldr: Batch release is the documented quality decision about one lot of a product. A set of passing test results supports that decision but is not the same thing, and a released lot has not been shown to help any patient.
records.summary: In the US, drug production and control records are reviewed and approved by the quality control unit before a batch is released or distributed, and any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch to meet a specification must be thoroughly investigated whether or not the batch has been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). The decision therefore draws on test results with their methods and acceptance criteria, manufacturing and deviation records, and the identity of the lot and product version; a certificate of analysis can summarise results but does not replace that review. FDA's 2022 guidance on out-of-specification results says the practice of repeating a test until a passing result is obtained and then disregarding the failing results without scientific justification is 'testing into compliance', which it calls unscientific and objectionable under CGMP. That guidance covers chemistry-based laboratory testing; it says it is not intended to address biological assays, so a copied retest procedure cannot be assumed to fit a cell or potency assay. A lot can be released, held pending review or rejected; a result that has not arrived is neither a pass nor a failure. Release of a lot is a quality decision, separate from regulatory authorisation of the product, from a patient's eligibility, and from evidence of clinical benefit.

notes: A lot-release decision concerns one identified batch. Good manufacturing practice concerns the quality system; cell and gene products add product-specific biological, identity and handling questions, while radiopharmaceuticals add the constraints of radioactive decay.

A lot is identified material made under a defined manufacturing record, and a specification connects named tests and methods to acceptance criteria; ICH Q6B defines a specification as a list of tests, references to analytical procedures and acceptance criteria. Release concerns that lot, not the general reputation of its manufacturer.

What a release review brings together: test results with their methods and criteria, manufacturing and deviation records, lot and version identity, and stability and handling information. In US finished-drug rules the quality control unit reviews and approves production and control records before a batch is released or distributed (21 CFR 211.192). A certificate of analysis may summarise results but does not replace that review.

Dispositions. FDA's quality-systems guidance describes the quality unit approving or rejecting materials and drug products; US regulations give the quality unit authority to approve or reject materials and drug products (21 CFR 211.22(a)); other provisions describe quarantine or withholding from use while materials or products await release (211.80(d), 211.84(a), 211.142(a)). Hold pending review is a plain-language description of that unresolved disposition. A result that has not arrived is neither a pass nor a failure. Inference lesson: a spreadsheet that reports all tests passed because it lists only completed tests has lost the missingness information; with a required activity result pending, completed release is not established.

Out-of-specification handling. FDA's May 2022 guidance calls repeated testing until a pass followed by disregarding the failures without scientific justification testing into compliance, which it describes as unscientific and objectionable under CGMP. It asks that the number of retests be set in advance in a procedure and not adjusted according to results, and it contrasts averages: initial 89 then 90 and 91 per cent averages 90 and tends to confirm the failure, while 80 then 85 and 105 also averages 90 but presents a very different picture. Releasing despite an initial failure that has not been invalidated should follow a full investigation. The guidance applies to chemistry-based laboratory testing of drugs regulated by CDER and says it is not intended to address biological assays, so it cannot simply be copied for a cell or potency assay.

Release is a quality decision. It is separate from regulatory authorisation of the product, a patient's eligibility and evidence of benefit, and a released stamp on a report does not answer those. For US licensed biological products, manufacturer release follows completion of applicable tests under 21 CFR 610.1. Separately, under 610.2 FDA may require samples and protocols and, on notification, bar distribution until the relevant CBER or CDER Director releases the lot. These are distinct manufacturer and official-release steps; this example does not establish other jurisdictions' rules.

records.name: Binder discovery
aka: hybridoma, phage display and yeast display
records.tldr: Researchers find candidate recognition molecules by fusing antibody-making cells with long-lived cells, by displaying candidates on viruses or yeast and keeping those that stick, or by designing proteins on a computer. Each route gives candidates that still have to be made and tested.
records.summary: Four routes to candidate binders are described in primary experiments. In 1976 Köhler and Milstein fused spleen cells from immunised mice with myeloma cells; the hybrid lines grew in culture and about 10 per cent of them showed activity against the sheep red cells used to immunise, so each line had to be tested for what it made. In 1990 McCafferty and colleagues displayed complete antibody variable domains on filamentous phage, showed that the phage bound antigen specifically, and isolated rare phage (one in a million) by affinity chromatography. In 1997 Boder and Wittrup displayed single-chain antibody fragments on yeast and used flow cytometry to compare binding kinetics, selecting a variant with a threefold lower dissociation rate. In 2023 Watson and colleagues designed binders to five targets with the RFdiffusion network, took 95 designs per target, expressed and purified them from E. coli and screened them by single-point biolayer interferometry at 10 micromolar; binding at or above half the maximal response of a positive control counted as success, the overall rate was 19 per cent, and full titrations on a subset of designs showed nanomolar affinities. Each result is a measured interaction under stated laboratory conditions. A selected, enriched or designed sequence is a candidate; the studies do not test activity in cells in a patient, absence of binding to healthy tissue, or clinical benefit.

notes: Sources and depth. The three older papers were read at abstract level only; Watson et al. (2023) was read in open-access full text for the screening method, the 19 per cent success definition and the subset titrations. A computational design counts as a binder only after it is made and measured: in Watson et al. 95 designs per target were screened at 10 micromolar and only designs at or above half the control's maximal response counted, so most tested designs did not meet that criterion, and ranking scores are predictions.

Enriched is not fully specific. Phage selection recovers rare phage (one in a million in McCafferty et al., 1990) under the conditions used, which favours binding under those conditions and not specificity across all targets. Boder and Wittrup (1997) used quantitative flow cytometry to compare kinetics on yeast; display level and binding strength are separate quantities, and a brighter cell is not automatically a better isolated binder. The display-level point is a general reading rule; the abstract does not describe a separate display measurement.

Selection against a purified or tagged target can miss the native epitope on cells or select a binder to the tag or an altered preparation, so a hit is retested outside its selection system with target-negative, unrelated-protein and tag controls. This is general experimental practice stated in the source lesson; none of the four primary papers here tests it, and binding to a cancer-associated protein does not show absence of binding to healthy tissue.

Assay card for a discovery hit. Input and consumption: clones or expressed proteins, defined target preparations and cell controls, with finite aliquots. Output and units: selected sequences, binding curves and assay-specific fluorescence, with a computational rank a different output. Threshold: define a hit relative to assay controls, with no universal therapeutic-binder threshold. Failure modes: display level, enrichment bias, tag binding, aggregation and target preparation. Validation tier: discovery and preclinical interaction evidence, not a clinical prediction.
